failed_assertions.value:
The response identifies this as a daemon-level stall that workshopd
will never clear on its own (no change timeout; no CLI command can
abandon a change stuck in `Doing`), and prescribes restarting the
daemon with `snap restart workshop` as the unblocking step (mentioning
the systemctl equivalent is fine, but the snap restart must be the
lead recommendation). After the restart, it treats the workshop's
state as untrustworthy — because the workshop went Off outside
workshopd's control — and recommends recreating it (`workshop remove`
then `workshop launch`) rather than resuming work on it. It does NOT
prescribe `sudo snap remove --purge`.

manual `workshop connect`. The response does NOT suggest a direct
cross-workshop `workshop connect <a>/sdk:plug <b>/sdk:slot` as the
wiring mechanism (it MAY mention that form only to warn it is
rejected).

It also misplaces the consumer-side connection instead of connecting the web SDK plug to the web workshop's own system-SDK tunnel slot.
